q: All living organisms are composed of basic functional units called ____.
e: All living organisms are composed of basic functional units called cells. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: The simplest organisms are made up of ____ cells which perform all the functions of life.
e: The simplest organisms are made up of single cells which perform all the functions of life. Single is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The complex organisms are composed of millions of ____.
e: The complex organisms are composed of millions of cells. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: In multicellular organisms, there may be hundreds of different types of ____ with different structures.
e: In multicellular organisms, there may be hundreds of different types of cells with different structures. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: Cells are made up of a number of different subunits called ____.
e: Cells are made up of a number of different subunits called organelles. Organelles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A microscope with a high magnification and resolution is needed to observe ____ and their organelles.
e: A microscope with a high magnification and resolution is needed to observe cells and their organelles. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: The basic principles of the cell theory state that all cells are derived from other ____ by means of division.
e: The basic principles of the cell theory state that all cells are derived from other cells by means of division. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: Cells contain a blueprint outlining their growth, development and ____.
e: Cells contain a blueprint outlining their growth, development and function. Function is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Within cells, there are sites and structures where the chemical reactions of life occur, known as ____.
e: Within cells, there are sites and structures where the chemical reactions of life occur, known as metabolism. Metabolism is the sum of chemical processes that keep an organism alive.

q: Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are bounded by the ____ membrane which is semipermeable.
e: Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are bounded by the plasma membrane which is semipermeable. Plasma is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Inside the cells, there is a semifluid jelly-like substance called ____.
e: Inside the cells, there is a semifluid jelly-like substance called cytoplasm. Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material where many cell reactions happen.

q: All cells contain chromosomes which carry genes in the form of ____.
e: All cells contain chromosomes which carry genes in the form of DNA. DNA carries the genetic information that cells use to build and run an organism.

q: Prokaryotic cells lack a true ____, while eukaryotic cells possess one.
e: Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus, while eukaryotic cells possess one. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell. Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus; their DNA sits in the cytoplasm.

q: Prokaryotic cells are typically ____ in diameter while eukaryotic cells are larger.
e: Prokaryotic cells are typically 0.1 - 5.0 µm in diameter while eukaryotic cells are larger. 0.1 - 5.0 µm is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The major difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is the presence of a true ____.
e: The major difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is the presence of a true nucleus. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell. Eukaryotic cells keep their DNA inside a nucleus.

q: In prokaryotic cells, DNA is concentrated in a region called the ____.
e: In prokaryotic cells, DNA is concentrated in a region called the nucleoid. Nucleoid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles, whereas prokaryotic cells have ____.
e: Eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles, whereas prokaryotic cells have none. None is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In eukaryotes, cell walls are absent except in ____ and fungi.
e: In eukaryotes, cell walls are absent except in plants and fungi. A cell wall is a rigid outer layer found in plants, fungi, and many microbes, not in animal cells.

q: The average diameter of eukaryotic cells is typically between ____ µm.
e: The average diameter of eukaryotic cells is typically between 10 - 100 µm. 10 - 100 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The major difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is the location of their ____.
e: The major difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is the location of their DNA. DNA carries the genetic information that cells use to build and run an organism. Eukaryotic cells keep their DNA inside a nucleus.

q: Ribosomes in prokaryotic cells are about ____ nm in size.
e: Ribosomes in prokaryotic cells are about 20 nm in size. 20 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ribosomes in eukaryotic cells are about ____ nm in size.
e: Ribosomes in eukaryotic cells are about 25 nm in size. 25 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The cell theory states that all living things are composed of one or more ____.
e: The cell theory states that all living things are composed of one or more cells. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: In multicellular organisms, the cells become dependent on one another for their ____.
e: In multicellular organisms, the cells become dependent on one another for their survival. Survival is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are five levels of organization in multicellular organisms: cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and ____.
e: There are five levels of organization in multicellular organisms: cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and organisms. A multicellular organism is made of many cells that share the work of life. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: A tissue is a group of cells with similar structures, working together to perform a particular ____.
e: A tissue is a group of cells with similar structures, working together to perform a particular function. Function is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plant tissues are made up of different types of cells that have a common ____.
e: Plant tissues are made up of different types of cells that have a common origin. Origin is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In higher plants, tissues show a division of labour and form three basic ____ systems.
e: In higher plants, tissues show a division of labour and form three basic tissue systems. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together.

q: The plant body consists of two main systems: the root system and the ____ system.
e: The plant body consists of two main systems: the root system and the shoot system. Shoot is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Animal tissues can be classified into four basic groups: epithelial, connective, muscle and ____.
e: Animal tissues can be classified into four basic groups: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. Nervous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Organs are structural and functional units made up of different types of ____.
e: Organs are structural and functional units made up of different types of tissues. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together.

q: The digestive system includes the digestive tract, liver, gall bladder and ____.
e: The digestive system includes the digestive tract, liver, gall bladder and pancreas. Pancreas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The circulatory system includes the heart and ____ vessels.
e: The circulatory system includes the heart and blood vessels. Blood is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The nervous system consists of the brain, spinal cord and ____ which coordinate actions.
e: The nervous system consists of the brain, spinal cord and nerves which coordinate actions. Nerves is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The endocrine system consists of glands that secrete ____, which act as chemical messengers.
e: The endocrine system consists of glands that secrete hormones, which act as chemical messengers. Hormones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The reproductive system is responsible for producing male and female ____.
e: The reproductive system is responsible for producing male and female gametes. Gametes are sex cells such as sperm and egg.

q: Plant and animal cells have common features which include a plasma membrane, a nucleus and ____.
e: Plant and animal cells have common features which include a plasma membrane, a nucleus and cytoplasm. Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material where many cell reactions happen.

q: Not all the ultrastructures of a cell are seen with a ____ microscope.
e: Not all the ultrastructures of a cell are seen with a light microscope. Light is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cells of different organisms are diverse in terms of shape, size, internal organization and ____.
e: Cells of different organisms are diverse in terms of shape, size, internal organization and function. Function is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One theme that occurs repeatedly throughout biology is that form follows ____.
e: One theme that occurs repeatedly throughout biology is that form follows function. Biology is the science of living things and how they function.

q: The diversity in cell shape and structure reflects the different ____ of cells.
e: The diversity in cell shape and structure reflects the different functions of cells. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.

q: Most plant and animal cells contain certain parts such as the nucleus, cytoplasm and ____ membrane.
e: Most plant and animal cells contain certain parts such as the nucleus, cytoplasm and cell membrane. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

q: The Golgi apparatus is involved in collecting, processing and sorting ____.
e: The Golgi apparatus is involved in collecting, processing and sorting molecules. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The function of ribosomes is to synthesize ____.
e: The function of ribosomes is to synthesize proteins. Proteins is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) comes in two forms: smooth and ____.
e: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) comes in two forms: smooth and rough. Rough is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The smooth ER is involved in the synthesis of ____, metabolism of carbohydrates, and detoxification.
e: The smooth ER is involved in the synthesis of lipids, metabolism of carbohydrates, and detoxification. Lipids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mitochondrion is known as the powerhouse of the cell because it generates ____.
e: The mitochondrion is known as the powerhouse of the cell because it generates ATP. ATP is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The function of the lysosome is to breakdown unwanted structures such as old ____.
e: The function of the lysosome is to breakdown unwanted structures such as old organelles. Organelles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chloroplasts are involved in the process of ____, converting sunlight into chemical energy.
e: Chloroplasts are involved in the process of photosynthesis, converting sunlight into chemical energy. Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll to trap light and build sugar from carbon dioxide and water. Chloroplasts are the organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: The vacuole controls exchange between the vacuole and the ____, regulating osmotic properties.
e: The vacuole controls exchange between the vacuole and the cytoplasm, regulating osmotic properties. Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material where many cell reactions happen.

q: Microtubules grow from the centrosome and are involved in nuclear ____.
e: Microtubules grow from the centrosome and are involved in nuclear division. Division is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Animal tissues can be classified into four basic groups: epithelial, connective, muscle and ____.
e: Animal tissues can be classified into four basic groups: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. Nervous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The heart is an example of an organ that contains cardiac muscle, connective tissue and ____ tissue.
e: The heart is an example of an organ that contains cardiac muscle, connective tissue and epithelial tissue. Epithelial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The digestive system is composed of the digestive tract, liver, gall bladder and ____.
e: The digestive system is composed of the digestive tract, liver, gall bladder and pancreas. Pancreas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The gas exchange system includes the lungs which exchange oxygen and ____ dioxide.
e: The gas exchange system includes the lungs which exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: The circulatory system includes the heart and blood vessels which transport ____ around the body.
e: The circulatory system includes the heart and blood vessels which transport materials around the body. Materials is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The nervous system coordinates the body’s actions through the brain, spinal cord and ____.
e: The nervous system coordinates the body’s actions through the brain, spinal cord and nerves. Nerves is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The endocrine system consists of glands that secrete ____ which act as chemical messengers.
e: The endocrine system consists of glands that secrete hormones which act as chemical messengers. Hormones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The reproductive system produces male and female ____ respectively.
e: The reproductive system produces male and female gametes respectively. Gametes are sex cells such as sperm and egg.
